questions.stem: What is the primary reason for the development of IPv6?
questions.explanation: IPv6 was developed primarily to provide more IP addresses. IPv4, with its 32-bit address space, can support approximately 4.3 billion unique addresses, which is insufficient for the growing number of internet-connected devices. IPv6 uses a 128-bit address space, vastly increasing the number of available addresses. While improving security and reducing congestion are important, they were not the primary motivations for IPv6.
